answer.rationale: The two live deficits are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there can cascade. Both memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifting completion/time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifting SMB activation) point at this lever, which is exactly why they are the two worth spending the verification budget on: they are the load-bearing claims for the action I intend, and the consolidated summaries have clearly been stripped of caveats. Notice that only memory_73 still carries its scope qualifier ('measured in the standard SMB segment') — the others assert clean wins with no segment, effect size, duration, or holdout details. That asymmetry suggests consolidation dropped qualifiers rather than that no qualifiers existed, so I want the original records for memory_86 and memory_31 before committing rather than treating 'durable lift' as established. I am deliberately not chasing the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 records a 12% retention cost against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and matching entry pricing would be the fastest way to buy acquisition that does not persist. referral_incentive (memory_57) is sound but targets established customers, not the leaking top of funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the one under pressure; activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strongest fallback and is my switch if verification shows the onboarding records were thin, narrow, or confounded. Key downstream value risk to instrument, not just note: cutting signup fields and shortening onboarding can inflate activation counts while degrading lead qualification and self-serve fit, converting a real revenue-quality loss into an apparent funnel win. So the experiment runs with a holdout and is judged on qualified pipeline, 60–90 day retention, and expansion — not completion or activation rate alone — with a pre-committed rollback if quality metrics move against us. Scale is a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout precisely because the supporting evidence is summary-level and unverified at the time of writing.
